claims.text: Pre-oxidizing the FeNiCrCoCu coating can form a continuous, adherent surface oxide scale.
A continuous, adherent oxide scale will significantly enhance the high-temperature wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Annealing in air at 700°C for 1 hour is the proposed pre-oxidation treatment.
The engineered oxide layer will primarily comprise Cr-rich and Cu-rich oxides.
The engineered oxide layer will be continuous and strongly adherent to the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The oxide scale reduces direct contact between the coating and the opposing surface.
The oxide scale minimizes oxidative degradation during wear.
The oxide scale acts as a mechanically robust barrier that distributes applied stresses more evenly.
Reduced direct contact, reduced oxidative degradation, and more even stress distribution enhance overall high-temperature wear resistance.
The pre-oxidized coating will have a lower friction coefficient than the unoxidized coating under identical high-temperature, high-load conditions.
The pre-oxidized coating will have a lower wear rate than the unoxidized coating under identical high-temperature, high-load conditions.
The pre-oxidized coating will have greater surface hardness than the unoxidized coating.
The protective oxide scale will remain intact without significant spallation throughout the wear tests.
The hypothesis is intended to apply at temperatures from 500°C to 700°C under high mechanical loads.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under lower-temperature or low-load conditions.
